home.faq1Answer: Yes. Free tests cost nothing: sign in and sit them, checked instantly. Premium adds the whole library, the explanations behind every answer, and more AI feedback.
home.faq2: How is my score worked out?
home.faq2Answer: Listening and Reading answers are checked against the key and converted with the official tables: to an IELTS band from 0 to 9, or to the Multilevel scale out of 75 (65+ is C1, 51+ B2, 38+ B1).
home.faq3Answer: Yes, a free one. Anyone can look through the tests, but you sign in with Telegram or Google to sit one: every result is kept, and Writing and Speaking can be marked.
home.faq4: Is it like the real exam?
home.faq4Answer: The sections, timings, part structure and question types follow each exam's official format. IELTS sits on the computer-delivered IELTS screen; Multilevel on a screen laid out the way that exam is.
home.faq5: Does it work on my phone?
home.faq5Answer: Yes. Every test works on a phone: on small screens the passage and the questions switch with one tap.

level.C1: You use English flexibly and effectively for social, academic and professional purposes, and follow long, demanding texts.
level.B2: You interact with fluency and spontaneity and understand the main ideas of complex texts. C1 starts at 65.
level.B1: You deal with most everyday situations and understand the main points of clear, standard English. B2 starts at 51.
level.A2: You understand sentences and common expressions on familiar topics. B1, the first level the exam certifies, starts at 38.

ieltsLevel.C2: Band 8.5+ (C2): you use English fully and flexibly, with only rare slips.
ieltsLevel.C1: Band 7–8 (C1): you handle complex language well, with occasional inaccuracies.
ieltsLevel.B2: Band 5.5–6.5 (B2): you use English effectively, though with some errors and misunderstandings. Many universities ask for 6.5.
ieltsLevel.B1: Band 4–5 (B1): you manage in familiar situations but make frequent mistakes. Band 5.5 is the next step.
ieltsLevel.A2: Below band 4: you understand basic English in familiar situations. Keep building vocabulary and grammar.

seat.title: Exam seat
seat.enterCodeText: The six digits the invigilator gave you at check-in.
seat.faceToFace: Face to face, with the examiner
seat.doneText: Your results are announced by whoever runs this mock. Press Finish to leave the computer ready for the next candidate.
seat.waitText: Sit quietly: the invigilator opens the next section for the room.

mocks.title: Mock sessions
mocks.lead: Run a mock on your own computers, like the real test: check candidates in, give each a seat code, open the sections for the room, and announce the results as a report with a QR code.
mocks.notYet: Mock sessions are for teachers and learning centres
mocks.notYetText: A teacher's account runs its own sessions; a centre's owner and teachers run the centre's while its licence runs. Ask us to make your account a teacher's.
mocks.noneText: Make one: pick a test, a time and a room.
mocks.holdText: Candidates see their marks only once you announce them.
mocks.noCandidatesText: Add the centre's students, or register walk-ins at the desk.
mocks.slipHow: At any computer in the room, type this code. It works once, while the session runs.
mocks.noStudents: Every student of the centre is in this session already.
mocks.seen: Left the page {away}× · pasted {pastes}× · left full screen {fs}×
mocks.noCreditsText: A session can be made once there are mock credits to check candidates in. Buy credits on Telegram; they are added to your centre or your account.
mocks.deleteText: Nobody has begun it, so it goes with its candidates.

objective.title: AI analysis
objective.introReading: Why you lost marks, not just where: the patterns behind your mistakes, a technique for your weakest question types, and the paraphrases you missed. About half a minute.
objective.introListening: Why you lost marks, not just where: the patterns behind your mistakes, a technique for your weakest question types, and what the speakers said in other words. About half a minute.
objective.perfect: Everything right: nothing to fix here. Try a harder test, or a whole section against the clock.
objective.paraphrasesHelp: The questions rarely use the passage's words: these say the same thing.
objective.paraphrasesHelpListening: The questions rarely use the speakers' words: these say the same thing.
objective.guide: An AI analysis to guide your practice; your mark is the one above.
